mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns: a 1% increase in FEDFUNDS compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates, predicting negative 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5.0%, it signals monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations, predicting negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or the rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) combined with a low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.5%) signals aggressive monetary tightening in a tight labor market, predicting negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with tight labor market
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and UNRATE < 4.5%, or the rank IC between the interaction signal and returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a decline in housing starts (HOUST < 1650.0) and retail sales (RSAFS < 351240.0) signals weakening demand, predicting negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1650.0 and RSAFS < 351240.0, or the rank IC between the interaction signal and returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100.0) signals weakening economic activity, predicting negative 5-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The rank IC between INDPRO and 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 5-day return is positive when INDPRO < 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 205.0, it signals accelerating inflation, predicting negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to anticipated monetary tightening.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 205.0, or the rank IC between CPIAUCSL and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100.0) and housing starts (HOUST < 1650.0) signals a weakening economy, predicting negative 60-day S&P 500 returns through reduced demand and earnings.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0 and HOUST < 1650.0, or the rank IC between the interaction signal and returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A tightening labor market (UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS > 136826.0) signals strong economic growth, predicting positive 20-day S&P 500 returns due to elevated corporate earnings and confidence.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS > 136826.0, or the rank IC between the interaction signal and returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
